name: OSS-Fuzz-Gen (LLM fuzz target generation)
one_liner: An LLM writes a fuzz target for under-fuzzed code, OSS-Fuzz builds and runs it, and build errors go back to the model.

loop.proposes: Fuzz targets (C/C++ entry points) for functions that Fuzz Introspector flags as under-fuzzed
loop.judged_by: OSS-Fuzz build; whether the target calls the function, start-up crashes and new line coverage are reported metrics
loop.steers: Build errors go back to a code-fixer prompt; repeated rounds fix errors

headline_result: Google's page reports 14 of 31 tested OSS-Fuzz projects compiled new targets and increased coverage (gains 0 to 31%; tinyxml2 line coverage 38% to 69%), and a similar target in OpenSSL rediscovered CVE-2022-3602.
caveat: The page calls this a preliminary investigation on a small set of C/C++ benchmarks with an unnamed Google model. The 14 are the projects that succeeded and the selection of the 31 is not fully explained. Calling-the-function, crash and coverage results are reported metrics; the page does not say they feed back into the model.
beyond_harness_note: The product is a fuzz target that keeps running in OSS-Fuzz without the model, but the in-loop checker here is the OSS-Fuzz build, not a formal authority; calling the function, start-up crashes and coverage are reported metrics.
generative_model: Google LLMs (model not named on the page)
algorithmic_authority: OSS-Fuzz build tooling; calling the function, start-up crashes and coverage are reported metrics

sources.title: Fuzz target generation using LLMs (OSS-Fuzz research docs)

verification.notes: Opened Google's OSS-Fuzz research page; undated but linked to an August 2023 announcement. Brief said 'build and coverage feedback loop': the page only documents build errors (and a not-calling-target error) returned to the LLM; coverage is a measurement, not shown as feedback. Later versions of the open-source repo may differ and were not checked. 'OSS-Fuzz-gen' 2023 year is inferred from the linked announcement.
